description:
We are a creative and ambitious team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are passionate about space exploration, engineering, technology, and innovation. We are working on an educational strategy game called "Moon Base Builder: Survival Strategy", where players take on the role of NASA engineers and face the challenges of building a sustainable lunar base.

We are looking for motivated team members interested in programming, game development, UI/UX design, science research,
summary:
We developed an educational strategy game that simulates the challenges of building a sustainable human base on the Moon. Players take the role of NASA engineers and make critical decisions about landing sites, energy, water, oxygen, and astronaut protection, based on NASA scientific research.


Our game transforms complex lunar science and engineering challenges into interactive learning experiences. Players use NASA-based scientific information to compare lunar locations, manage limited resources, design habitat protection, and respond to environmental hazards. It helps students understand the decisions required to support future lunar missions

Returning humans to the Moon requires scientific knowledge, engineering skills, and careful resource management. Our project makes these challenges easier for young learners to understand through gameplay, encouraging scientific curiosity, strategic thinking, and interest in space exploration.
details:
What the Project Does:

It is a simple, interactive simulation game called "Moon Base Builder", inspired by NASA's 2028 Artemis mission to the Moon. It puts kids and students in the shoes of a "junior space engineer" to design and protect a lunar base at the South Pole against extreme cold (down to -203^\circ\text{C}) and rocket weight limits.

How it Works & Learning from Mistakes:

Players don't just pick materials blindly. They learn about the trade-off (inverse relationship) between material efficiency (like Aerogel vs. Aluminum), shield thickness, and payload weight. If a player makes a wrong choice, the app doesn't just say "wrong"—it explains why it failed, helping them learn through trial and error.

The Impact:

Through this simple tool, complex space and physics concepts are made super easy, significantly increasing the percentage of kids who understand space science.

Tools, Languages & How They Are Used

Language Used:

Python: The core programming language used to write the code and control the game's logic (checking whether the shield succeeds or fails based on thickness and material).

Files & Tools Used:

Streamlit Library (Framework): Used to create a clean, easy-to-use web interface featuring control sliders (st.slider), selection buttons, and instant educational feedback messages.

Main File (app.py): A single Python file containing the simulation logic and user controls.

Environment: Runs smoothly inside any web browser.
